summary: Karin Preisendanz specializes in Indology and philosophy. She completed her Dr. phil. and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg. Her academic career includes posts at the University of British Columbia (1990–1993) and a professorship at the University of Vienna from 1999.

Karl Albert Agathon Benary was a scholar in linguistics and other fields who studied at Halle and Göttingen (Ph.D. 1824–1827), later studying under Franz Bopp. He served as a Gymnasiallehrer at Cöllnisches Gymnasium (1833–1860) and Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin (1839).

Karl Ammer was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (1930–1939), studying under Bernhard Geiger, Erich Frauwallner, Nikolai Trubetzkoy, and Wilhelm Havers. He held posts in Vienna before becoming professor and institute director at Halle (1954–1970).

Karl Benedikt Hase worked in linguistics and history. He studied at Jena, Helmstedt, and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. His career included posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, École des langues orientales vivantes (1816–1864), École Polytechnique, and the University of Paris.

Karl Bernhard Seidenstücker worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his Ph.D. at Leipzig under Ernst Windisch after studies at Göttingen and Halle. He founded several Buddhist organizations, served as secretary of the Maha Bodhi Society, and worked at the Museum am Rothenbaum.

Linguist Karl Bohnenberger earned his Ph.D. at the University of Tübingen (1881–1886) under Rudolf von Roth and Eduard Sievers. He spent his career in Tübingen as a librarian (1888–1921) and professor of German language (PD from 1892; ord. Professor 1921–1930).

Linguist and Indologist Karl Brugmann studied at Halle, Bonn, and Leipzig, completing his doctorate under Georg Curtius. He served as Ordinarius at the University of Freiburg (1884) and subsequently as professor at the University of Leipzig from 1887 to 1919.

Karl Brunnhölzl is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued traditional studies under Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Khenpo Lama Thubten.

Karl Debreczeny specializes in Tibetology and art history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Hung Wu and Jenny Purtle. He served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2008).

Karl Dyroff was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology who attended the Kronberg Gymnasium Aschaffenburg. He held an academic appointment at the University of Munich from around 1900 to 1934.

Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal was a scholar in history and other fields. He studied at Leipzig, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Heidelberg University, where he later held an academic post from approximately 1842 to 1845.

Karl Eugen Neumann was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Berlin and Halle, and earned his Ph.D. at Leipzig (1890–1891) under Richard Pischel, also studying with Ernst Windisch, Paul Deussen, Wilhelm Grube, Albrecht Weber, and Hermann Oldenberg.

Karl Felix Halm was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He held joint posts in Munich from around 1856 to 1882 at the University of Munich and as an official at the Bavarian State Library.

Karl Ferdinand Johansson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University under Olof August Danielsson and Per Persson. He spent his career at Uppsala University, serving as Privatdozent, extraordinary professor, and ultimately professor from 1908 to 1925.

Karl Florenz was a scholar of Japanology, Indology, and linguistics who earned his Ph.D. at Leipzig under Ernst Windisch. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1889–1917) and held a chair at the Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut and University of Hamburg (1914–1935).

Karl Friedrich Burkhard was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Erlangen, Munich, and Halle (PhD 1845–1846). He held teaching posts at Evangelisches Gymnasium Teschen and Akademisches Gymnasium Wien, and served as director of Franz-Joseph-Gymnasium Wien (1874–1890).

Karl Friedrich Geldner studied Indology and Iranian languages at Leipzig and Tübingen, earning his Ph.D. under Rudolf von Roth. He held chairs at the University of Halle, Humboldt University of Berlin (1890), and the University of Marburg (1907–1921).

Karl Friedrich Hermann was a scholar of history and classical antiquity who studied at Heidelberg under Friedrich Creuzer and Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann. He held academic posts at Heidelberg University (~1826–1832), the University of Marburg (~1832–1842), and the University of Göttingen (~1842–1855).

Karl Friedrich Keil studied theology and Oriental languages at the University of Tartu and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp. He served as Privatdozent and then Professor of Exegetics and Oriental Languages at the University of Tartu (1838–1858).

Karl Friedrich Neumann worked in Sinology and history. He studied at Heidelberg, Göttingen, Munich, San Lazzaro degli Armeni, and under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat. He served as professor at the University of Munich (1833–1852) and curator at the Bavarian State Library (~1833–1863).
